name: CrossGET
backbones: CLIP (ViT-B/16 vision tower); BLIP; BLIP2-OPT-2.7B/6.7B; LLaVA-1.5-7B; LLaVA-1.5-13B
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: >98% of the original average over 10 benchmarks at 2382.5 forward GFLOPs (baseline 4480.9), forward throughput 60.4 vs 32.0
notes: ICML 2024. Reduction inside the transformer layers of both the vision and the language branch (module placed between self-attention and FFN); same number of tokens combined per layer. Importance comes from learnable cross tokens that proxy the other modality, not from the per-sample text prompt, so not marked query-aware. Main tables are after tuning (CLIP fine-tuned; BLIP2: ViT+Q-Former tuned; LLaVA-1.5: LLM+projector tuned on 10% SFT data, ViT frozen); a w/o-tuning variant is also reported (Table 6, Fig. 4). Throughput reported but GPU and batch size not stated.
evidence: "This framework adaptively combines tokens in real-time during inference" (Abstract); "CrossGET jointly considers the token similarity derived from intra-modal complete-graph soft matching and the token importance indicated by cross-modal guidance to determine which tokens should be combined" (Fig. 1 caption); "The number of tokens is reduced to half with the same reduction number for each layer" (Sec. 4.1); "the only part of CrossGET that requires training is learning cross tokens. However, they are initialized with informative features ... Therefore, CrossGET can also be used without training (certainly worse than with training)" (Sec. 4.3)

name: PruMerge / PruMerge+ (LLaVA-PruMerge)
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: PruMerge+ VQAv2 76.8 / POPE 84.0 / MME 1462.4 (baseline 78.5 / 85.9 / 1510.7) with 25.0% of visual tokens on average; PruMerge 72.0 / 76.3 / 1350.3 with 5.5%
notes: ICCV 2025 (arXiv v1 Mar 2024). Reduction at the vision-encoder output before the projector: CLS attention of the penultimate CLIP layer selects outlier tokens (IQR rule, so the count varies per image), pruned tokens are merged into the kept ones by kNN on last-layer keys with class-attention weights; PruMerge+ adds spatially uniform tokens. LLM untouched. Main Table 1 uses LoRA fine-tuning of LLaVA-1.5 for 1 epoch (light); training-free results in Table 6 and for Video-LLaVA. Table 2 prefill time is a roofline estimate on V100, not measured. No code URL in the arXiv text.
evidence: "we exploit the sparsity observed in the visual encoder, characterized by the sparse distribution of attention scores between the class token and visual tokens. This sparsity enables us to dynamically select the most crucial visual tokens to retain. Subsequently, we cluster the selected (unpruned) tokens based on their key similarity and merge them with the unpruned tokens" (Abstract); "we adopt the Interquartile Range (IQR) method [5] ... Any attention values residing outside these fences are classified as outliers" (Sec. 3.2); "PruMerge can be conducted in either a training-free or fine-tuning manner" (Sec. 4.4.3); "We further finetune LLaVA-1.5 using LoRA [19] for 1 epoch" (Sec. 4.1)

name: FastV
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-13B: 4-task average 73.6 (baseline 73.6) at 84.6 GFLOPs (baseline 154.6) with K=2, R=50%
notes: ECCV 2024 (oral). Prunes inside the LLM: after layer K (default K=2) image tokens are ranked by the average attention they receive from all other tokens (text tokens included, so prompt-dependent) and the lowest R% are dropped for all later layers. K=0 variant drops randomly before the LLM. Latency per example on one A40 (Table 4, K=0 R=50%); batch size not stated.
evidence: "FastV implements an image token pruning strategy at one specific layer of LLM. Prior to this layer, computations proceed as usual. Beyond this selected layer, image tokens are re-evaluated based on their average received attention scores" (Sec. 1); "The last R% tokens after ranking would be pruned out in successive layers. We simply compute the average attention-score one token received from all other tokens as the criteria" (Sec. 4.1); "FastV is plug-and-play to different token-based LVLMs for various vision language tasks without the need of training the model" (Sec. 4.1)

name: SparseVLM
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: 99.1% of average accuracy over 8 benchmarks with 192 of 576 tokens at 2.14 TFLOPs (baseline 4.62), latency 36.50 ms (baseline 57.82)
notes: ICML 2025. Prunes inside the LLM decoder layers progressively: visually relevant text tokens (raters) are chosen before the LLM, visual tokens are scored by the rater-to-vision attention logits, the per-layer count N = lambda*(Lv - rank(P)) varies per image, and pruned tokens are recycled by density-peak kNN clustering into a few reconstructed tokens. Latency on one A100-80GB with single-image inputs; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we propose a text-guided training-free token optimization mechanism dubbed SparseVLM that eliminates the need of extra parameters or fine-tuning costs ... we select relevant text tokens to rate the significance of visual tokens using self-attention matrices and, then, prune visual tokens" (Abstract); "we introduce a rank-based strategy to adaptively determine the sparsification ratio for each layer, alongside a token recycling method that compresses pruned tokens into more compact representations" (Abstract); "N = lambda x (Lv - rank(P)). We then remove N visual tokens with the smallest values in P" (Sec. 3.2)

name: VisionZip
backbones: LLaVA-1.5-7B; LLaVA-1.5-13B; LLaVA-NeXT-7B; LLaVA-NeXT-13B; Mini-Gemini; Video-LLaVA
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: 94.0% of average score over 11 benchmarks with 64 of 576 visual tokens (training-free), 95.2% after projector tuning; LLaVA-NeXT-7B: prefilling 27.8 ms vs 218 ms with 160 of 2880 tokens
notes: CVPR 2025 (doi 10.1109/cvpr52734.2025.01843). Reduction at the vision-encoder output (layer -2 features) before the projector: dominant tokens chosen by CLS attention (mean received attention for SigLIP), remaining tokens merged by key similarity into contextual tokens; text-agnostic, LLM unchanged. Training-free by default; VisionZip-dagger tunes only the projector (light, 30 min on 8 A800). Efficiency on one A800-80GB; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we first select the dominant tokens, which receive significant attention and aggregate most of the image information. Then, to avoid missing small but potentially important details, we employ a token merging strategy, merging retained tokens based on their similarity to further extract informative contextual tokens" (Sec. 1); "Our method can be used in training-free, fine-tuning, or training from scratch" (Sec. 1); "we use minimal instruction tuning data to efficiently fine-tune the multimodal projector while keeping other components frozen" (Sec. 2.4)

name: ViCo (PyramidDrop, PDrop)
main_result: LLaVA-NeXT-7B: 7-benchmark average 70.5 (baseline 70.9) at 9.5 TFLOPs (baseline 20.8), inference-only; LLaVA-1.5-7B: 96.8% of average with 192 average tokens
notes: CVPR 2025 under the title Conical Visual Concentration for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models (ViCo); arXiv 2410.17247 is titled PyramidDrop (PDrop). Prunes inside the LLM at the end of each of S=4 stages (every 8 layers of a 32-layer LLM) with ratio lambda=0.5, ranked by attention between the last instruction token query and image keys (FlashAttention compatible). Used both as a training-free inference strategy and inside LLaVA training (40% training-time reduction). Inference cost reported as FLOPs only; training GPU hours are wall-clock.
evidence: "we partition the LVLM into several stages and drop part of the image tokens at the end of each stage with a pre-defined ratio. The dropping is based on a lightweight similarity calculation" (Abstract); "we calculate the attention between all the image tokens and the last token of the instruction" (Sec. 3.2); "PyramidDrop can also serve as a plug-and-play strategy to accelerate inference in a free way" (Abstract); "PyramidDrop can achieve over 40% training time reduction" (Abstract)

name: DivPrune
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: GQA 56.85 / MMB 59.19 / POPE 86.02 (baseline 61.96 / 64.09 / 85.84) at 15.63% of the original TFLOPs
notes: CVPR 2025. Prunes after the projector, before the first LLM decoder layer (Layer 0); text-agnostic max-min diversity (cosine distance) selection solved greedily; ablation shows pruning at later LLM layers is worse. Prefill and end-to-end latency on V100 32GB with batch size 1.
evidence: "we first formulate token pruning as Max-Min Diversity Problem (MMDP) where the goal is to select a subset such that the diversity among the selected tokens is maximized" (Abstract); "DivPrune is a training-free, calibration-data-free, plug-and-play solution" (Sec. 1); "By default, in our method, visual tokens are pruned before being passed to the first decoder layer in the LLM" (Sec. 4.6); "All results are obtained with a batch size of 1" (Sec. 4.1)

name: CDPruner
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: 99.0% of average over 10 benchmarks with 128 of 576 tokens, 97.0% with 64, 94.3% with 32; LLaVA-NeXT-7B: prefill 38 ms vs 246 ms with 320 of 2880 tokens
notes: NeurIPS 2025 (Crossref: Advances in NeurIPS 38, doi 10.52202/085713-0855); arXiv v2 says under review. Prunes after the projector before the LLM: DPP kernel of cosine similarity between visual tokens, re-weighted by instruction relevance (CLIP text vs. vision features for LLaVA; projector output vs. mean instruction embedding for Qwen2.5-VL), greedy MAP in O(n m^2). Needs no attention maps (FlashAttention compatible). Latency on one A100-80GB on POPE; batch size not stated.
evidence: "We first define the conditional similarity between visual tokens conditioned on the instruction, and then reformulate the token pruning problem with determinantal point process (DPP) to maximize the conditional diversity of the selected subset. The proposed CDPruner is training-free and model-agnostic" (Abstract); "we calculate the cosine similarity to measure the relevance r between each visual token and the instruction" (Sec. 3.3)

name: VTW
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: MME 1872.43 / POPE 85.96 (baseline 1866.10 / 85.83) at 4.68 TFLOPs (baseline 8.48) with K=16
notes: AAAI 2025. Inside the LLM: all vision tokens are withdrawn after layer K (K=16 for 7B, 20 for 13B), no per-token scoring; K is searched offline per model/dataset as the first layer whose KL divergence to the full model is below eta=0.003 on 20 samples. KV-cache and FlashAttention compatible. Latency per example of LLaVA-NeXT-7B on one RTX 3090 (0.33 s vs 0.52 s); batch size not stated.
evidence: "we strategically withdraw them at a certain layer, enabling only text tokens to engage in subsequent layers. To pinpoint the ideal layer for VTW, we initially analyze a limited set of tiny datasets and choose the first layer that meets the Kullback-Leibler divergence criterion" (Abstract); "VTW serves as a seamless extension to off-the-shelf pre-trained MLLMs, requiring no extra training cost" (Experimental Setting)

name: HiRED
main_result: LLaVA-NeXT-7B: TextVQA 61.4 / DocVQA 60.8 / MME 1483 (baseline 64.8 / 73.4 / 1519) with a 20% token budget; 2.30 vs 0.49 tokens/s and TTFT 4.21 s vs 19.49 s on a Tesla P40
notes: AAAI 2025. Drops tokens at the vision-encoder output before the projector/LLM for high-resolution (multi-partition) VLMs: a fixed total token budget is split across the full image and sub-images by layer-0 CLS attention (content score), then top tokens per partition are kept by final-layer (22) CLS attention. Schedule marked budget because the total is a fixed budget while the per-partition split is adaptive. Throughput/latency/memory on Tesla P40 at batch sizes 1, 2, 4.
evidence: "HiRED leverages the attention of CLS token in the vision transformer (ViT) to assess the visual content of the image partitions and allocate an optimal token budget for each partition accordingly. The most informative visual tokens from each partition within the allocated budget are then selected and passed to the subsequent Large Language Model" (Abstract); "a plug-and-play token-dropping method designed to operate within a fixed token budget" (Abstract); "plug-and-play integration (i.e., without model training and architectural changes)" (Sec. 1)

name: TokenPacker
main_result: LLaVA-1.5-7B: 6-benchmark average 62.8 (baseline 62.0) with 144 of 576 visual tokens, LLM throughput 24.9 vs 4.9 tokens/s on one A100
notes: IJCV 2025 (doi 10.1007/s11263-025-02491-7); arXiv 2024. Reduction at the projector between encoder and LLM: features from before the last CLIP layer are bilinearly downsampled by s (s=2,3,4 gives 144/64/36 tokens) as point queries and refined by cross-attention over multi-level high-resolution region features. Learned projector with no token scoring, so criterion is none. Trained with the LLaVA-1.5 recipe (projector pretrain, then LLM + projector instruction tuning, vision encoder frozen). Throughput (tokens/s) on one A100; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we first interpolate the visual features as a low-resolution point query, providing the overall visual representation as the foundation. Then, we introduce a region-to-point injection module that utilizes high-resolution, multi-level region-based cues as fine-grained reference keys and values" (Abstract); "We adjust the down-sampling ratio s in {2, 3, 4} in TokenPacker to control the quantity of generated visual tokens" (Sec. 4.1); "we maintain vision encoders fixed across both stages, while focusing on optimizing our proposed TokenPacker. Concurrently, the optimization of the LLM is exclusively conducted during the instruction-tuning phase" (Sec. 4.1)

name: FEATHER
backbones: Prismatic-style VLM: SigLIP ViT-SO400M + MLP + Llama-2-7B
main_result: SigLIP-SO400M + Llama-2-7B: >5x the localization average of FastV at 64% FLOPs reduction (FastV 68%); Table 1 K=8 ensemble criterion: localization average 35.6 vs 23.3 for the FastV criterion at 50% FLOPs reduction
notes: ICCV 2025. Prunes inside the LLM in two stages: after layer 8 keep (1-R) of visual tokens by attention from the last text token computed without RoPE plus uniformly sampled tokens (stride 3), after layer 16 keep (1-R)^2 by the RoPE-free attention alone (R=0.75). Main finding: FastV's criterion is biased to bottom-of-image tokens by RoPE long-term decay, which hurts localization and TextVQA while most benchmarks do not notice. Only FLOPs reported. No code URL in the paper; arXiv comment gives a project page (https://web.stanford.edu/~markendo/projects/feather).
evidence: "we propose a straightforward modification to the attention-based criteria by removing RoPE, demonstrating that this resolves the positional bias issue and greatly improves performance. Additionally, we incorporate uniform sampling in early token pruning to ensure adequate coverage of all image regions and apply more extensive pruning at a later layer" (Sec. 1); "we first perform pruning after an early layer (K = 8), utilizing our proposed criteria phi-R + phi-uniform to retain (1 - R)% of tokens ... we additionally prune a second time at K = 16" (Sec. 4.2); "In this work, we study the inference acceleration of VLMs where visual tokens are pruned within the attention mechanism of LM" (Sec. 3.1)

name: EffiVLM-Bench
main_result: LLaVA-OneVision-7B: VisionZip keeps 0.75 of overall performance at a 1% token budget vs 0.48 for FastV; at 40% FastV 0.94 and VisionZip 0.93
notes: ACL 2025. Benchmark, not a method. Evaluates training-free acceleration on 17 benchmarks (DocVQA, ChartQA, TextVQA, OCRBench, AI2D, GQA, MMMU, MME, RealworldQA, MMStar, MathVista, LLaVA-Wilder, MMBench, MMVet, ImageDC, MP-DocVQA, MovieChat) with metrics for performance, generalization, loyalty and measured inference time: token pruning (FastV, VisionZip, PruMerge+), KV-cache compression (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, LOOK-M, VL-Cache) and parameter compression (EcoFLAP, Wanda, SparseGPT, AWQ, GPTQ). Findings: token compression is task-dependent and collapses at a 1% budget on OCR and long-output tasks; pruning in the vision encoder (VisionZip, PruMerge+) beats pruning in the LLM (FastV) at low budgets; KV-cache methods have better generalization and loyalty but little TTFT speedup, token pruning gives up to 3.2x TTFT speedup; parameter compression keeps performance better but does not shorten inputs. Batch size 1; efficiency on one A800 with 8k input tokens. Only a project page URL is given.
evidence: "We introduce EffiVLM-Bench, a unified framework for assessing not only absolute performance but also generalization and loyalty, while exploring Pareto-optimal trade-offs" (Abstract); "Token compression performance is task-dependent and shows significant sensitivity to benchmark and model. Most methods are stable at higher budgets but degrade sharply at 1%" (Sec. 4.1, Observation 1); "For token pruning on a 1% budget, pruning tokens within the visual encoder (e.g., VisionZip and PruMerge+) consistently outperforms those pruning in the LLM backbone (e.g., FastV)" (Sec. 4.1); "KV cache compression outperforms token pruning in generalization and loyalty" (Sec. 4.1, Observation 2)

name: FitPrune
main_result: LLaVA-NeXT-7B: 5-benchmark average 66.8 (baseline 67.1) at 15.6 TFLOPs (baseline 34.1) with a 60% pruning ratio
notes: AAAI 2025. Prunes inside the LLM at every layer following a per-layer recipe (cumulative counts t_i) found offline by binary search so that the FLOPs budget is met while the self- and cross-attention distributions of visual tokens change least; statistics from 655 LLaVA-665k samples (about 5 min on one A100 40G). At inference tokens are ranked by received self-attention times received cross-attention from text tokens (prompt-dependent). Throughput in samples/s (Tables 4, 7); batch size not stated.
evidence: "FitPrune considers token pruning as a statistical problem of MLLM and its objective is to find out an optimal pruning scheme that can minimize the divergence of the attention distributions before and after pruning. In practice, FitPrune can be quickly accomplished based on the attention statistics from a small batch of inference data" (Abstract); "we propose a novel and training-free method called fit-and-prune (FitPrune), which consider token pruning as a task of cross-distribution fitting" (Introduction); "During inference, tokens are ranked by the combined importance metric a_u = a_s * a_c" (Method)
